title: Revenue tile shows Parts and Labor as whole percentages, or the invoice count
custom_preconds:
1. Sign in on the build under test as an Admin user. Admin holds every permission, including Reports, so Reports and Dashboard both show in the top menu.
  2. In the top bar, click the location name at the top left (e.g. ShopHub) and choose your test location: one where nobody else invoices, issues credits or clocks time this week. The next step checks that it is quiet. If no location you can reach is quiet, create one once and reuse it on every later run: Settings > Locations > add a location (e.g. "ZZAUTOTEST Dashboard Quiet") > save, give your user access, then choose it here. Locations cannot be deleted, so never create a second one.
  3. Check the location is quiet: click Dashboard in the top menu, click the range pill on the Revenue tile and choose This Week. Revenue must read $0.00 with 0 Invoices under it. If it shows anything else, choose another location.
  4. Run the whole case on one day, and not on the last evening of the week, so every record you create stays inside This Week.
  5. Create a test customer: Customers > New Customer, name it (e.g. "ZZAUTOTEST Dash Customer 1") and save. On its Contacts tab add a contact (e.g. "Dana Test"). On its Assets tab add an asset (e.g. unit "ZZ-101") and pick that contact in the asset's Contact field. If the customer's edit screen shows Default Shop Supplies, set it to 0 so the invoice carries only labor and parts.
  6. Have an in-stock inventory part to sell: Parts > Inventory, pick (or create with New Inventory Part) a part with stock on hand and a Sell price of e.g. $100.00. Credits are issued by returning a part, so the credit needs this part on the invoice.
  7. Prepare (do not invoice yet) one work order for this customer with these standard steps:
    • Work Orders > New Work Order > choose the customer and its asset > Create.
    • In the work order header set Service Advisor to "Alex Advisor" and enter the mileage (e.g. 123456). If the Finance tab is greyed out with "Please select a contact for the asset", choose the contact and answer YES to keep it on the asset.
    • Lines tab > New Line: Description "ZZAUTOTEST Labor 2h", Technician "Tom Tech", Labor Rate e.g. $100.00 per hour, Estimated Time 2.00, Tech Time 2.00, tick Approved > Save & Close.
    • On that line click + Add Part, choose the inventory part (Sell price e.g. $100.00), quantity 1, and make sure it shows In stock (pick it if the screen asks).
    • On each line type a Story (e.g. "Done") and set the line to Complete. Then click Complete Work Order, then Mark Reviewed.
custom_steps:
1. Click Dashboard in the top menu, set the Revenue tile's range pill to This Week and read the line under the amount.
  2. Click Work Orders, open the prepared work order, click the Finance tab and click Create Invoice. Close the New Customer Payment dialog without paying.
  3. On the invoice write down the labor total and the parts total (e.g. Labor $200.00 = 2.00 hours x $100.00, Parts $100.00). If the invoice also shows shop supplies, write that amount down too.
  4. Work out the split by hand: Parts = $100.00 / ($100.00 + $200.00) x 100 = 33.33, shown as 33. Labor = $200.00 / $300.00 x 100 = 66.67, shown as 67.
  5. Click Dashboard, set Revenue to This Week again and read the line under the amount.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Before the invoice: Revenue reads $0.00 and the line under it reads "0 Invoices", because there is no parts-and-labor split to show.
  • After the invoice: the line reads "Parts 33% · Labor 67%", each a whole number (33.33 rounds to 33, 66.67 rounds to 67), and the two add up to 100.
  • If the invoice carried shop supplies and your percentages differ only because of them, mark the case Blocked and write all three amounts in the comment: the specification does not say which side shop supplies fall on.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-490; story SV-9576 (S4); Dashboard v1 PRD, Confluence 788430850 v42, read 7 Oct 2026, S4 (S4-R3, S4-N2), S3 (S3-E3, Revenue split sentence). Design canvas (claude.ai/artifact/Wae9DFQ8PJQBy8mbLsL5ge, captured 2026-09-28) used for on-screen labels and navigation only: boards 02_Last12_After ("Parts 7% · Labor 93%"), 15_Empty_Design ("0 Invoices").

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S4-R3: “The Revenue tile shows a supporting line reading "Parts {parts}% · Labor {labor}%", each percent shown as a whole number.”
  • S4-N2: “If the Revenue tile has no parts-versus-labor split to show, its supporting line reads "{count} Invoices" instead.”
  • S3-E3 (Revenue split sentence): “The same applies to the Revenue tile's parts-versus-labor split when revenue for the range is zero (S4-N2 already gives that tile its fallback supporting line).”

Last checked against build v26.39.1-09be696 on 10/2/2026.
